value_chain.value_chain_position: Databricks sits at the data infrastructure layer, bridging raw data storage and AI/analytics workloads. It depends on the three major cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) for underlying compute and storage infrastructure, and on NVIDIA GPUs for its Mosaic AI model serving capabilities. Upstream, it integrates data from enterprise sources (databases, data lakes, streaming). Downstream, it serves data engineers, data scientists, ML engineers, and business analysts who build data pipelines, train models, and run analytics. With its Mosaic AI suite and foundation model partnerships (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google), Databricks increasingly extends into the model serving and orchestration layers, making it a multi-layer platform that connects data infrastructure to AI application development. Its Lakehouse architecture directly competes with Snowflake's data warehouse and with cloud-native analytics offerings from AWS (Redshift), Google (BigQuery), and Azure (Synapse).

key_products: Databricks Lakehouse Platform: unified data analytics platform combining data lake flexibility with data warehouse performance, built on Apache Spark and Delta Lake. Supports ETL/data engineering, SQL analytics (Databricks SQL), streaming, and machine learning workloads on a single platform. Unity Catalog provides unified governance across all data and AI assets, including Delta and Iceberg tables, unstructured data, and ML models. Runs on AWS, Azure, and GCP with serverless compute options.

Mosaic AI: full-stack AI/ML suite built from the $1.3B MosaicML acquisition. Includes Agent Bricks (auto-optimized AI agents for enterprise use cases), Foundation Model APIs (serving DBRX and third-party models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral), AI Vector Search (billions of vectors at 7x lower cost), model training/fine-tuning infrastructure, and MLflow 3 for generative AI monitoring. Enables enterprises to build, deploy, and govern AI applications on their own data.

Unity Catalog: industry's first unified governance solution for all data and AI assets. Provides discovery, search, lineage, quality monitoring, and business semantics across Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, unstructured data, and AI models. Open-sourced in 2024, works across formats, engines, and clouds, positioning Databricks as the neutral governance layer in multi-cloud environments.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Revenue run-rate of $4.8B as of Q3 2025 (September 2025), growing >55% YoY. Includes >$1B AI products revenue run-rate and >$1B data warehousing revenue run-rate. Previous milestone: $4B run-rate in June 2025. Private valuation: $134B (Series L, December 2025), up from $100B (Series K, August 2025) and $62B (Series J, December 2024). Still private, but CEO has not ruled out a 2026 IPO.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: $4.8B annualized revenue run-rate as of September 2025, up from $3.0B at end of 2024. AI revenue run-rate exceeded $1B. Data warehousing revenue run-rate exceeded $1B. Growing >55% YoY with positive free cash flow over the trailing 12 months.
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Total raised: ~$19.3B over 14 rounds. Last round: Series L, >$4B at $134B valuation (December 2025), led by Insight Partners, Fidelity, J.P. Morgan Asset Management, with participation from a16z, BlackRock, Blackstone, Coatue, GIC, MGX, NEA, Ontario Teachers, Robinhood Ventures, T. Rowe Price, Temasek, Thrive Capital, Winslow Capital. Previous major rounds: Series K $1B at $100B (August 2025), Series J $10B at $62B (December 2024).
business.business_model: Usage-based consumption pricing via Databricks Units (DBUs), a normalized compute unit. Customers pay per-second for compute resources consumed, priced by workload type (SQL analytics, data engineering, ML, serverless), cloud provider, region, and pricing tier. Open-core model: open-source foundations (Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow) attract adoption, while proprietary features (Photon engine, Delta Live Tables, serverless, Mosaic AI, managed Unity Catalog) drive paid consumption. Revenue is primarily from platform usage on customer cloud accounts. Also earns from Mosaic AI foundation model serving (pay-per-token). Positive free cash flow achieved in 2025.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Free cash flow positive over trailing 12 months as of Q3 2025. No longer burning cash. With $19.3B raised and FCF-positive operations, runway is not a concern. Potential 2026 IPO would provide additional liquidity.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Hybrid. Databricks champions open-source as core strategy: Apache Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow, and Unity Catalog are all open-source projects created or maintained by the company. However, the managed platform, Photon engine, Delta Live Tables, serverless compute, Mosaic AI, and advanced Unity Catalog features are proprietary. DBRX foundation model released under Databricks Open Model License. Open formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg) ensure data portability, but performance optimizations and governance features create stickiness to the proprietary platform.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: Databricks is one of the most important companies for entrepreneurs building data-intensive or AI-powered products to understand, for several reasons: (1) The Lakehouse architecture represents the convergence of data warehousing and data lakes into a single platform -- startups no longer need to choose between the two, reducing infrastructure complexity and cost; (2) Databricks' open-source strategy (Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow, Unity Catalog) means startups can start with free open-source tools and graduate to the managed platform as they scale, avoiding vendor lock-in at the data layer; (3) Mosaic AI and Agent Bricks enable startups to build enterprise AI agents on their own data without managing ML infrastructure, lowering the barrier to adding AI features to products; (4) The partnership ecosystem with Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google means startups building on Databricks can access multiple foundation models through a single governed platform, simplifying model selection and compliance; (5) Databricks' $134B valuation at 55%+ growth demonstrates that data infrastructure remains one of the most valuable layers of the AI value chain -- investors see data platforms as durable businesses rather than commoditized infrastructure; (6) For startups selling to enterprises, Databricks is often already present in the data stack of target customers, making integration a competitive advantage; (7) The competitive dynamics between Databricks and Snowflake are driving rapid innovation and price competition, which benefits startups as consumers of these platforms; (8) Unity Catalog's open-source governance model is becoming an industry standard, and startups building data products should understand this emerging paradigm.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Highly accessible for startups. Databricks for Startups program offers up to $50,000 in platform credits plus free business-tier technical support for VC-backed startups. AI Accelerator Program (invitation-only) provides up to $250K in Databricks Ventures funding plus product credits and mentorship. Free 14-day trial available for anyone. Open-source foundations (Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow) can be self-hosted at zero cost. Pay-as-you-go pricing with per-second billing means no minimum commitment. Serverless options eliminate infrastructure management overhead. However, the full managed platform can become expensive at scale, and the startup program requires VC funding to qualify.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None for core data platform. Mosaic AI integrates multiple foundation models via partnerships: Anthropic (Claude, $100M deal, March 2025), OpenAI ($100M deal, September 2025), Google (Gemini, June 2025), plus Meta Llama and Mistral models. Also offers its own DBRX open model. The platform is model-agnostic by design.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: Cloud providers: Microsoft Azure (Azure Databricks since 2017, deepest integration), AWS (major partnership, 'Buy with AWS' integration since December 2024), Google Cloud (expanded partnership June 2025). Foundation model providers: Anthropic (5-year, $100M partnership, March 2025), OpenAI ($100M partnership, September 2025), Google/Alphabet (4-year Gemini integration, June 2025). Key investors include Andreessen Horowitz, BlackRock, Insight Partners, Thrive Capital, and sovereign wealth funds (GIC, Temasek, MGX). Acquisitions bolster the ecosystem: MosaicML ($1.3B, AI models), Tabular (Apache Iceberg), Neon ($1B, Postgres), Tecton (real-time AI features), BladeBridge (data migration), Mooncake (real-time analytics).
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Open-source ecosystem lock-in: Databricks created or maintains Apache Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow, and Unity Catalog -- the most widely adopted open-source data and ML tools. This gives them enormous community credibility and a funnel of developers already familiar with their stack. The Lakehouse architecture positions data warehousing as a use case within the data lake, commoditizing Snowflake's core business. Multi-cloud neutrality allows Databricks to serve as the unifying data platform across AWS, Azure, and GCP. The $19.3B in funding enables aggressive M&A (6 acquisitions in 2024-2025 alone) to fill platform gaps faster than competitors. Unity Catalog's governance layer creates switching costs once enterprises adopt it for data and AI asset management. The Mosaic AI suite with multiple foundation model partnerships makes Databricks the Switzerland of enterprise AI, avoiding dependency on any single model provider.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: Exempt from EU AI Act as a data infrastructure platform -- Databricks does not develop or deploy its own general-purpose AI models (DBRX is open-weight and small-scale). Positioned as an enabler of compliance rather than a regulated entity: Unity Catalog provides governance, lineage, and access controls that help customers meet EU AI Act and GDPR requirements. Databricks has European data center regions and has committed to European data sovereignty. Primary regulatory exposure is around data protection (GDPR, CCPA) as a data processor, not as an AI provider. If Databricks were to IPO in 2026, it would face SEC reporting obligations. No DMA gatekeeper risk.
